gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured brightness for any projector that works without Wi-Fi: TechGearLab measured the Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 (no Wi-Fi, no smart OS) at 2,061 ANSI lumens against Epson's 3,000-lumen ISO rating, about ten times the 200 lumens Aurzen rates the ZIP Pro at.
standout_why: I read nexttools.net and innovativeprojector.com in full. Neither names a mainstream model with a measurement: nexttools names no projector at all, and innovativeprojector names only its own K7X Pro, with no figures. I could not read the body of the TechRadar TCL PlayCube review (rank 17): WebFetch returned only the title, on both the US and SG URLs. So I can't rule out that it states a figure. The aurzen.com ZIP Pro page (rank 2) returned HTTP 429. The Epson, Philips, ION and Laser Corp FAQ and manual results are maker documents, which don't contain third-party measurements. ChatGPT's answer showed the CO-W01 only as '3,000 lumens' and gave no measured figure.
decides: The CO-W01 is the clearest fit for 'no Wi-Fi'. Epson's US page lists no built-in Wi-Fi or smart OS, and Projector Reviews found streaming needs an external device on HDMI. TechGearLab and Projector Reviews both measured it above 2,000 ANSI lumens in normal modes, so it is the pick for a lit room. The Aurzen ZIP Pro works offline over USB-C video input, and Notebookcheck says the Wi-Fi login at setup is optional. But it is rated at only 200 lumens, and Notebookcheck measured 2 h 10 min of movie playback, so it suits dark rooms and travel. CGMagazine says the TCL PlayCube's first-time setup has to be done over Wi-Fi, which counts against it for this shopper.

findings.label: Measured brightness (TechGearLab)
findings.source_title: Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 Review - TechGearLab
findings.note: Sentry Kelly (with Adam Stout), review dated 2024-03-22. Measured with a light meter. Epson rates it at 3,000 lumens (ISO), so the measurement is about 69% of the rating.

findings.label: Measured input lag (TechGearLab)
findings.source_title: Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 Review - TechGearLab
findings.note: 1080p signal, measured with an input-lag test device. Average of readings at the top, middle and bottom of the screen. Review dated 2024-03-22.

findings.label: ANSI contrast (TechGearLab)
findings.source_title: Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 Review - TechGearLab
findings.note: ANSI checkerboard test with a light meter. 638 / 23 = 27.7. Epson publishes no contrast figure.

findings.label: Fan noise (TechGearLab)
findings.source_title: Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 Review - TechGearLab
findings.note: TechGearLab lists the figure without describing a method. It equals the 38 dB on ProjectorCentral's spec page, so it may be the spec rather than a measurement.

findings.label: Measured brightness by picture mode (Projector Reviews)
findings.value: Dynamic 3,457 / Presentation 2,698 / sRGB 2,428 / Cinema 2,279 / Vivid 2,279 / Blackboard 1,704 ANSI lumens
findings.source_title: Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 Portable Projector Review - Projector Reviews
findings.note: Kam Valentine, 2023-08-02. Full-white pattern at High light output, 3-4 readings taken 15-20% away from the lens center. The text also gives a 3,624 peak in Dynamic, which contradicts the table, so I used the table.

findings.label: Smart OS and inputs (Projector Reviews)
findings.value: No smart OS; HDMI (ARC), USB-A, USB-B; streaming needs an external device on HDMI
findings.source_title: Epson EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 Portable Projector Review - Projector Reviews
findings.note: The review's spec sheet says smart functionality 'None' and networking 'No'. It doesn't say what the USB ports do.

findings.label: Maker price and brightness rating (Epson US)
findings.source_title: EpiqVision Flex CO-W01 Portable Projector | Epson US
findings.note: The page lists no built-in Wi-Fi or smart OS. It says 'Compatible with streaming' through an external device on HDMI.

findings.label: Measured battery runtime (Notebookcheck)
findings.source_title: Aurzen Zip Pro tri-fold 1080p projector review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: David Chien, published 2026-10-17, updated 2026-10-19. Movie playback in Normal brightness at 25% volume. The 2.5 h spec is for Eco mode. 38 Wh battery.

findings.label: Measured speaker loudness (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: 65.6 dBA (music) / 57.5 dBA (pink noise) at 1 m, max volume
findings.source_title: Aurzen Zip Pro tri-fold 1080p projector review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: This is speaker output, not fan noise. The fan-noise numbers in the article (24/28/35 dB) look like spec-sheet values.

findings.label: Offline wired input (Notebookcheck)
findings.value: USB-C 3.0 video input (DP Alt Mode), video latency up to 40 ms; Wi-Fi login optional at setup
findings.source_title: Aurzen Zip Pro tri-fold 1080p projector review - Notebookcheck
findings.note: AirPlay, Google Cast and Miracast casting need Wi-Fi. The AurzenHub app remote needs online registration. Brightness is listed as 100/150/200 lumens (Eco/Normal/Conference) in the spec table; Notebookcheck didn't measure it.

findings.label: Battery runtime in testing and Wi-Fi setup (CGMagazine)
findings.value: Close to 4 h continuous use; first-time setup must be done over Wi-Fi
findings.note: Kurston Timothy, 2026-06-17. The reviewer gave the runtime from his own use, without a fixed method. The '<26 dB' noise figure isn't marked as measured. The review lists one HDMI port and describes USB-C as for charging.
